# EconomicGrasp

[Run EconomicGrasp in five minutes](#run-in-five-minutes) from the authors' checkpoint: the weights, a first picture, the same from Python and in the browser, a first number on the benchmark. Then [the options of every slot](#the-slots): what fits where EconomicGrasp ships its components, and what was measured for each.

## Run EconomicGrasp in five minutes {#run-in-five-minutes}

From the authors' checkpoint to grasps on a scene: on the command line, from Python or in a browser, then a first number on a part of the benchmark. Every command here is run by the test suite (by parsing it, on a toy detector, or on the files it needs); what each printed when it was measured is said under it, with the date, the commit and the machine. The numbers come from the method's [metafile](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/economicgrasp/metafile.yaml) and [five_minutes.json](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/docs/methods/five_minutes.json).

### 1. The weights {#run-weights}

GraspPanda publishes no weights for EconomicGrasp: the checkpoint is the authors', under their licence, and weights converted from it are not redistributed by the project. Download the authors' file yourself:

- **File**: `economicgrasp_realsense.tar`, from <https://github.com/iSEE-Laboratory/EconomicGrasp/releases/download/v1/economicgrasp_realsense.tar>
- **Licence**: MIT (the repository vendors operator code derived from a non-commercial project); trained on GraspNet-1Billion (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
- **SHA-256**: `33c99bf43d599bd259c53c090badd83771ca34b8bebdb4a27a9a45a80df32223`

Convert it once, from the root of your GraspPanda checkout (the converter is a tool of the repository; it is not installed with the package):

```bash
python -m tools.convert_checkpoint economicgrasp_realsense.tar economicgrasp_realsense.pth \
    --source-format economicgrasp --camera realsense
```

It writes `economicgrasp_realsense.pth`: every tensor of the authors' file under the name of the module that plays its role here, no value changed, with a note of the file it came from. A tensor left over or missing stops the conversion with a report; nothing is ever loaded partially.

### 2. Grasps on the example scene {#run-demo}

```bash
grasppanda demo economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights economicgrasp_realsense.pth --example --collision-filter
```

`--example` is the synthetic table-top scene that ships with GraspPanda: no dataset and no download. The command prints the config and its hash, how the weights loaded (every tensor matched, none missing), the test pipeline, the cloud, how many grasps the model predicted and how many the collision filter left (the config's variant `cd`: `ModelFreeCollisionFilter`), and the ten best grasps. It writes into `work_dirs/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/`:

- `grasps.npy`: the grasps that are left, `(G, 17)` float32 in the GraspNet layout, best first, camera frame, metres;
- `grasps.png` and `grasps.gif`: the cloud with the 30 best grasps, still and swinging around the scene;
- `example/`: the scene as files (`depth.png`, `rgb.png`, `mask.png`, `intrinsics.txt`).

Measured with the authors' checkpoint, converted: **14.0 s** for the whole command; 20,000 points to the model, sampled from 316,254 in the workspace; 1024 grasps predicted, 725 left after ModelFreeCollisionFilter (2026-10-15, commit `ea6268b`, one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs).

The scene files stand in for a camera. On your own depth image, as on these:

```bash
grasppanda demo economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights economicgrasp_realsense.pth \
    --depth work_dirs/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/example/depth.png \
    --intrinsics work_dirs/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e/demo/example/intrinsics.txt \
    --workspace -0.25 -0.2 0.35 0.25 0.2 0.8 \
    --collision-filter --out work_dirs/camera
```

EconomicGrasp was trained on clouds cropped around the objects; on a camera image, `--workspace` (a box in the camera frame, metres) or `--mask` does that crop. Units and frames, the depth scale and the intrinsics: [Your own camera](../user_guides/inference.md#your-own-camera).

### 3. The same from Python {#run-python}

```python
from grasppanda import GraspInferencer
from grasppanda.apis import example_scene

scene = example_scene()  # the scene of --example
inferencer = GraspInferencer(
    "economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e", "economicgrasp_realsense.pth"
)
grasps = inferencer(
    depth=scene.depth, intrinsics=scene.intrinsics,
    depth_scale=scene.depth_scale, mask=scene.mask,
    table_from_camera=scene.table_from_camera, collision_filter=True,
)
print(len(grasps), grasps.sort_by_score().to_graspnet_array()[:3])
```

It runs the demo's pipeline on the demo's input, so it returns the demo's 725 grasps (the test suite checks that the two give the same array, on a toy detector). `mask=` stands in for the segmentation the config crops the workspace with; on your camera, pass a mask from any segmentation or `workspace=(xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax)` in metres. The fields of a grasp and what else the call takes: [From Python](../user_guides/inference.md#from-python).

### 4. In the browser {#run-browser}

```bash
# ~/grasppanda_weights: the folder that holds economicgrasp_realsense.pth
grasppanda explore --weights-dir ~/grasppanda_weights
```

The page opens at <http://127.0.0.1:8765/>. In the **Run** tab choose EconomicGrasp: `economicgrasp_realsense.pth` is chosen for you by its name. Keep the example scene (or upload a depth image with its intrinsics), leave the collision filter on, and press *Run*: the page shows the picture, the best ten grasps, the counts through the post-processing and the command that does the same in a terminal. The server listens on your machine only, reads weights only from that folder and downloads nothing: [Run in the browser](../user_guides/inference.md#run-in-the-browser).

### 5. A first number on the benchmark {#run-test}

With GraspNet-1Billion on disk (`export GRASPPANDA_GRASPNET1B_ROOT=...`, see [Dataset preparation](../user_guides/datasets.md)), score the weights on every 64th frame of the seen test scenes, 120 frames:

```bash
grasppanda test economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --weights economicgrasp_realsense.pth \
    --opts data.test.dataset.split=test_seen data.test.dataset.frame_step=64 evaluation.num_workers=4
```

It prints AP, AP0.8 and AP0.4 for every variant of the config, `raw` (the predictions as they are) and `cd` (with the collision filter), and writes a result record per variant into the run directory under `work_dirs/`. Testing needs no derived asset; the evaluator extracts a cache from the dataset's object models the first time it runs, which the times below do not include.

| Weights, provenance | Collision filter | AP, 120 frames of test_seen | AP, whole seen split | Difference | Wall time, commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the authors' checkpoint, converted, `author-ckpt` | off | 68.75 | 69.28 ([record](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/economicgrasp/records/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e_author-ckpt_test_raw.json)) | −0.53 | 44 s, `ea6268b` |
|  | on | 70.11 | 70.83 ([record](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/economicgrasp/records/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e_author-ckpt_test_cd.json)) | −0.72 |  |

Provenance: `author-ckpt`, the authors' weights, evaluated by GraspPanda. Inputs: the workspace is cropped around the ground-truth segmentation (`gt_assisted: workspace`), as in the reference. On these 120 frames the AP is within 0.72 AP of the whole split, so the subset tells you quickly whether your installation gives what the records say; it is not a benchmark number. Measured on 2026-10-15 on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs.

The machine: one NVIDIA RTX A6000 (48 GB) shared with other jobs, an AMD EPYC 7262 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=3; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.7.1 with CUDA 11.8, spconv 2.3.8.

## The options of every slot {#the-slots}

Every slot of EconomicGrasp (`economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e`), what the method ships with there, the options that fit it and the ones that do not, each with what was measured: the cells of the [measured grid](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md) that replace that one slot of EconomicGrasp. The method itself: [its README](https://github.com/Daeda1used/GraspPanda/blob/main/configs/economicgrasp/README.md). The same lists, with every message whole, in a terminal or as JSON:

```bash
grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list            # every slot
grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list <slot> --json
```

**One run, seed 0, 20 iterations, 8 frames of one scene; a class counts verdicts, not accuracy.** No accuracy appears on this page, and none follows from it: a probe trains 20 iterations on 8 frames and shows whether a combination works, not how good it is.

How to read a row: *C R L P* are the four levels of the cell under EconomicGrasp, **composes**, **runs**, **learns** and **predicts** (✓ reached, ✗ not, ? undecided: *not checked* for a record of the first judge, *unstable, not repeated* for an unstable run nobody probed again). The *Class* of an option counts the methods under which it reached each level; levels with the same class are named together. A probe that predicted no grasp on any frame is greyed. The levels, the classes and their thresholds are defined on the measured page, [Measured classes](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md#measured-classes).

| Slot | Written as | Shipped | Fit | Do not fit | Not probed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| [View](#view) | `model.view` | `TemplateViewStage` (option `template-view`) | 19 | 2 | 0 |

| [Losses](#loss) | `model.<stage>.<term>_loss` | the losses of the method's stages | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| [Post-processing](#post) | `evaluation.variants.post` | no variant `post` (the config has cd, raw) | 14 | 0 | 1 |
